High Availability

Run SATOM as a primary/standby pair — see both nodes and their replication live, register the peer, switch between HA and standalone mode, and fail over by hand.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → System → High Availability (URL /high-availability/)

What is it?#

SATOM can run as two nodes: a primary whose database is read-write and a standby that follows it. The High Availability page is the cluster's own view: which nodes exist, which one is primary, whether the standby is actually receiving data, and — when the primary is lost — a guarded, manual way to promote the standby. Loading the page never contacts an appliance: it reads the local database and probes the peer over HTTPS.

This page is about SATOM's own nodes. HA pairs of FortiWeb or FortiADC appliances are registered on Appliances.

What does it do?#

  • Cluster architecture — one card per registered node (name, host, role, running code revision, database state and lag, when it last reported), with an arrow from each primary to each standby. In HA mode the arrow is labelled streaming ▸ / WAL replication + staged deploy; in Standalone mode it reads standalone / no replication. The lag itself is on the node cards. Click a card to load it into the node editor; Add node clears the editor.
  • Node-to-node architecture — a fixed reference table of the channels the nodes use and what each carries.
  • Deployment mode — switches between HA — two-node cluster and Standalone — single node.
  • HA nodes — the node registry: add, update and remove the peer, with each node's live role, revision and health.
  • Database replication & failover — live PostgreSQL streaming-replication state from this node, whether the scheduler is active here, the load-balancer probe, and Promote this node to PRIMARY on a standby.

How the two nodes stay in sync:

What Mechanism Direction
Database (settings, users, devices, everything in PostgreSQL) PostgreSQL streaming replication, configured in PostgreSQL itself. A cluster installed with install-satom.sh accepts the standby's connections only over TLS (hostssl), and replication additionally needs a client certificate issued by the cluster's internal CA (clientcert=verify-ca) primary → standby, continuous
Files under data/ (database bundles, device-config vault, per-device JSON, versioned source-of-truth store, node registry) satom-ha-datasync.timer — the standby pulls data/ with rsync over SSH every 5 minutes standby pulls from primary
Application code Software Update: standby first, then primary; optionally driven by the reconciler per node
Health and status probes HTTPS on port 8443 only, to a peer certificate that must verify; every request HMAC-signed with the node identity key (the key itself is never sent) both ways

Requirements#

  • users.manage and the Global ADOM.
  • Two SATOM nodes installed as a cluster, with PostgreSQL streaming replication between them. The deployment-mode switch does not build or remove replication; it only changes SATOM's behaviour.
  • The data-sync timer and its SSH key on the standby (set up at installation time in cluster mode — see Installation).
  • The node certificate for the 8443 channel, trusted by the peer (the system trust store or the internal CA): Node TLS.
  • Both nodes' clocks NTP-synchronised: a peer request whose signature timestamp is more than 120 seconds off is refused.
  • Both nodes on the same SATOM release for the peer views to authenticate (see Updating the pair).

Permissions#

All routes — viewing the page, changing the mode, editing the registry and promoting — require users.manage (legacy coarse key user_manage); in the default profiles only Administrator has it.

🔑Permission

Without users.manage the Administrator menu is hidden and /high-availability/ returns 403 Forbidden.

Role restrictions:

  • Save mode is disabled on the standby — the mode lives in the replicated settings and can only be written on the primary.
  • Promote this node to PRIMARY is shown only on a node that is a standby and in HA mode.

How to use#

Register the peer node#

  1. Open Settings → System → High Availability on the primary.
  2. Click Add node (or click an existing card to edit it).
  3. Fill in Node name (hostname), Host / LAN IP and optionally Label (optional).
  4. Click Save node. The flash reads HA node '<name>' (<host>) saved. It propagates to the peer on the next data sync; its live state is probed on this page.

The node you are on is always kept in the registry. To remove the peer, click Remove on its row in HA nodes; the current node has no Remove button.

Switch between HA and standalone#

  1. On the primary, in Deployment mode, pick HA — two-node cluster or Standalone — single node.
  2. Click Save mode. The flash reads Deployment mode set to HA. (or STANDALONE).

In Standalone, the staged-update safeguard, peer probing, failover and the data sync are all off, and updates apply directly to the node. If no mode was ever saved, SATOM uses HA when a peer is registered and Standalone otherwise.

Check that the standby is receiving data#

  1. Look at Database replication & failover. - On the primary: each connected replica with its state (streaming in green), sync mode and WAL lag in bytes. This node is PRIMARY but no replica is connected — the standby is not streaming. means replication is down. - On the standby: STANDBY receiving with the apply lag and the receive / replay positions.
  2. Scheduler on this node should be active on the primary and idle on the standby — scheduled actions fire only on the primary.
  3. In HA nodes, the peer's Health should be up. unreachable means the 8443 probe got no answer, or the peer's certificate was refused.

Fail over to the standby#

⚠️Warning

Only promote when the current primary is confirmed down. There is no quorum: promoting while the old primary is alive creates two primaries (split-brain).

  1. Open the High Availability page on the standby.
  2. In Manual failover, type this node's name exactly as shown (for example satom-2).
  3. Click Promote this node to PRIMARY.
  4. The flash reads Failover queued (<id>). The privileged runner is promoting this node to PRIMARY and starting the app — watch the status below. The Failover in progress panel shows the steps until success or failed.
  5. Point users and the load balancer at the new primary. Last failover on the card records the outcome.
  1. 1Confirmtype the node name; must be a standby in HA mode
  2. 2Queuethe request goes to the privileged runner
  3. 3PromotePostgreSQL leaves recovery (waits up to 30 s)
  4. 4Startweb service enabled/started, scheduler restarted
  5. 5Health check/healthz must answer 200 within 30 s

After a promotion the data sync on the new primary stops pulling by itself (it only runs on a standby). Re-attaching the old primary as a new standby is a PostgreSQL re-seed (pg_rewind or a new base backup) done outside SATOM.

Updating the pair#

Update the standby first, then the primary (Software Update). Peer requests are signed (X-SATOM-Node-Ts / X-SATOM-Node-Sig), and a node refuses the old static X-FM-Node-Key header. While only one node runs a release with signing, expect about a minute of not authenticated peer views until the other node catches up.

If the nodes use signed releases, install the trust anchor /etc/satom/release-trust.allowed_signers on both nodes and sign on the primary with sudo satom execute sign-release. An unsigned change to deploy/ does not stop the standby from updating: the application updates and only the root-side refresh is held, with a warning.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Node name (hostname) The node's name as SATOM reports it (its host name, or the FM_NODE_NAME environment variable when set). Yes satom-2
Host / LAN IP Address the other node uses to probe this one and to pull data from it. Yes 192.0.2.12
Label (optional) Free-text description. No rack B
Deployment mode HA or Standalone. Replicated; set on the primary. No HA
Confirm promotion This node's name, typed exactly. Yes (promote) satom-2

The registry is stored in data/ha_nodes.json and reaches the peer with the data sync. The deploy-automation switch (reconciler Manual/Auto) is on Software Update.

Example#

🧪Example — Losing the primary

The primary's host fails. On the standby, the HA nodes table shows the primary as unreachable and the replication card shows the receive position no longer moving. After confirming the primary host is really down, the administrator types satom-2 in Manual failover and clicks Promote this node to PRIMARY. The steps finish with this node is now the read-write PRIMARY; the load balancer's /healthz/primary check now returns 200 on this node and it takes traffic.

Result#

  • Registry changes rewrite data/ha_nodes.json on this node.
  • A mode change is stored in the replicated settings and applies to both nodes.
  • A promotion makes this node's PostgreSQL read-write, starts the web service and restarts the scheduler.
  • Mode changes, promotions and node registry additions, edits and removals each write an Audit Log entry.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: HA mode changes, promotions and node registry changes are audited, the architecture diagram no longer claims replication on a standalone node, and the shipped satom.service binds the application server to 127.0.0.1:8000, so port 8000 is no longer reachable from the peer (existing nodes get the new unit at their next update).

Troubleshooting#

"The deployment mode is stored in the replicated settings — change it on the PRIMARY node (this node's database is read-only)."#

Possible causes - You are on the standby.

Solution 1. Open the page on the primary and save the mode there.

"This node is not a standby — promotion is only valid on the node currently in recovery."#

Possible causes - The node is already primary, or the mode is Standalone (failover is disabled in standalone mode).

Solution 1. Promote from the standby's own page, in HA mode.

"Confirmation failed: type this node's hostname (<name>) exactly to promote it."#

Solution 1. Type the name shown in the message, with the same case, and submit again.

"Both a node name (hostname) and a host/IP are required."#

Solution 1. Fill in both Node name (hostname) and Host / LAN IP.

Peer shows "unreachable"#

Possible causes - The peer is down, or port 8443 is blocked between the nodes. (Port 8000 listens on 127.0.0.1 only once the node runs the current satom.service, so it is not a usable path between nodes.) - The node certificate or identity key is not set up. - The peer's certificate does not verify against this node's system trust store or the internal CA. The request is refused rather than sent unverified; the log reads peer TLS refused for <host>: peer TLS certificate did not verify ….

Solution 1. Check the peer service, then the firewall between the nodes. 2. Check Node TLS: install a certificate the other node trusts. 3. Only as a temporary emergency measure, set SATOM_PEER_TLS_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 in .env (encrypted but unverified retry); remove it once the certificate is fixed.

Verification - The peer's card shows a role, revision and up.

Peer views show "not authenticated"#

Possible causes - The two clocks differ by more than 120 seconds, so the peer refuses the request signature. - One node is not yet updated to the release that signs peer requests (during an update this lasts about a minute, until the standby catches up). - The identity key is not configured.

Solution 1. Synchronise both nodes with NTP and check the offset (timedatectl on each node). 2. Finish the update on both nodes.

Verification - /healthz called by the peer reports peer_authenticated: true, and the peer views show the peer's details again.

"This node is PRIMARY but no replica is connected"#

Possible causes - PostgreSQL replication on the standby is stopped or cannot connect.

Solution 1. Fix replication in PostgreSQL on the standby (outside SATOM).

Verification - A replica row in state streaming appears on the primary.

Files missing on the standby#

Possible causes - The data sync timer is stopped, the SSH key is missing, or the registry lists no peer. The sync logs a reason and exits non-zero when it cannot query its role or find the peer.

Solution 1. Check satom-ha-datasync.timer on the standby (see Services and timers).

Advanced#

Advanced Roles and probes
  • A node's role is read live from PostgreSQL (pg_is_in_recovery()), never stored.
  • The standby cannot write the replicated settings, so the page probes the peer's /healthz/primary and /healthz endpoints instead of trusting a stored report. If the probe fails but the primary sees a streaming replica from the peer's address, the peer is shown as standby with replicating (app unreachable).
  • /healthz/primary returns 200 on the primary and 503 on a standby — use it as the load-balancer health check so traffic only reaches the read-write node.
  • In standalone mode the peer is not probed and its card reads standalone mode — probe disabled.
Advanced Data sync details
  • Runs on the standby only; it is a no-op on the primary and in standalone mode.
  • The peer is chosen from data/ha_nodes.json by excluding this node's own IP addresses (not by host name).
  • rsync --delete mirrors data/ except jobs/, tmp/, update-requests/, update-status/, logs/, diagnostics/ and deep_jobs/. Anything deleted on the primary disappears from the standby; anything created only on the standby under data/ is removed by the next run. This is why deletions and uploads belong on the primary.
  • The SSH login is pinned to a read-only rsync of data/ and runs as the SATOM service account, not root.
  • The copy is rsync -a, so file modes travel with the files: the standby's device config vault and system bundles stay owner-only (0600 files in 0700 directories), as on the primary. satom diagnose data grades the standby the same way, and the update runner repairs it after each update. See Data and storage.
Advanced Promotion internals

The runner refuses to promote if PostgreSQL is not in recovery, promotes the cluster, waits up to 30 seconds for it to become read-write, enables/starts the web service, restarts the scheduler and waits up to 30 seconds for /healthz to answer 200. Automatic failover is deliberately not implemented. On a container installation promotion is not available from this page.
